transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump was in Florida Friday, where he held a rally in Daytona Beach.
It's part of a last-minute effort by Republicans to rally supporters before Tuesday's midterm elections.
You've got to go and vote.
You know, a lot of people, they see the polls and they're both doing so good.
You've got to vote.
Bad things happen when you get too confident.
So let's pretend they're one point down, okay?
Is that mine?
It sounds a little negative because they're doing actually very well, but you have to go and vote.
On Sunday, Trump will campaign in Iowa and Kansas, two states with critical Senate races.
Election officials say early voting is surging with just days before the midterm elections.
An analysis by the Associated Press shows more than 43 million Americans have already cast ballots.
That's almost 10 million more than at the same point in 2022.
Texas has seen a 50% increase with 6.3 million early votes cast.
North Carolina and Kansas have both recorded increases of more than 30%.
A grand jury in Texas has indicted an ICE officer accused of intentionally hitting a Mexican construction worker with his car earlier this month.
The man was later placed in custody with a broken leg.
Houston Public Media's Bianca Seward has our story.
Mario Alberto Morales was indicted for a second-degree felony offense of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Harris County District Attorney Sean Tiers says he hopes the indictment will send a message.
An ICE badge does not give you free reign to injure, kill or violate the constitutional rights of anyone.
An ICE spokesperson claimed the victim Miguel Para Hernandez ran in front of the agent's vehicle while they were trying to arrest a different man.
Para Hernandez's lawyer has disputed ICE's account.
Surveillance video of the incident shows the agent driving towards Para Hernandez as he runs away from the car and into a parking lot where the collision occurred.
For NPR News, I'm Bianca Seward in Houston.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has left no doubt that Canada is working to become the first associate member of the European Union.
As Dan Carpenschuck reports, Carney's statement came at the end of a two-day Canada-EU summit being held in Montreal.
It's still not clear exactly what an associate membership would look like, be called, or if it comes with any price tags.
Canadian and EU officials in Montreal did put the final touches on a number of negotiations, as well as commitments to a new, deeper alliance.
In his closing remarks, Carney said they were working toward the deepest possible partnership, which will be determined over the coming months.
He said the plan is to conclude negotiations in June of next year.
He will then join European Council meetings.
And in March, the European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and the Council President will convene a meeting of EU commissioners and Canada's federal cabinet.
The new partnership will also be presented to the European Union and the Canadian Parliament for a debate and a vote.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carpenschuck in Toronto.
And this is NPR News.
The independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced Friday it's closing down.
Officials blamed relentless official pressure for the action.
The paper launched in 1993 with help from Mikhail Gorbachev, a former president of the Soviet Union.
It was Russia's last major independent media outlet critical of the Kremlin.
Ancient Egyptians left clues for how they made mummies, but they were written in hieroglyphics.
Now archaeologists are using chemistry to help decipher the code, and Piers Pinghuang reports.
The ancient Egyptians mummified their dead, preserving their bodies for thousands of years.
Much of the process remains a mystery, so researchers at Marburg University in Germany decided to test samples from mummified heads and body parts found in museum and historical collections.
Ricardo Guirica, an Egyptologist, says that chemical analysis turned up substances new to their understanding of mummification, like extracts from aloe, which may shed light on at least one hieroglyphic symbol.
Maybe we can translate ankhimi, which was not very sure beforehand now as aloe.
Aloe surprised them because it wasn't native to ancient Egypt.
It likely came from trade with regions near Ethiopia or Arabia.
The findings are published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Pinghuang, NPR News.
In college football, DJ Lagway threw for 319 yards and four touchdowns to lead the Baylor Bears to a 41-9 route of UCF Friday night.
Lagway finished with 16 of 25 in passing.
Also Friday, Tulane beat Charlotte in overtime 38-31, and in the long-running Ivy League rivalry, Dartmouth beat Harvard 24-14.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump holds Daytona Beach, Florida rally urging supporters to vote before midterms
Early voting surges ahead of midterms, with over 43 million ballots cast nationwide
Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales over hitting Mexican construction worker
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney pursues associate membership in the European Union at Montreal summit
Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces it is closing under official pressure
Marburg University researchers use chemistry to find aloe in ancient Egyptian mummification
Baylor's DJ Lagway throws four touchdowns in 41-9 win over UCF
Tulane beats Charlotte 38-31 in overtime; Dartmouth defeats Harvard 24-14
